relations.subject: server:auto-reprovision
relations.evidence: This mechanism is not needed for Couchbase buckets because a Couchbase buckets data is persisted to disk and can be loaded back into memory after a node restarts.

relations.subject: server:auto-reprovision
relations.evidence: If ephemeral buckets are not in use this setting has no effect on the cluster.

notable_absence.finding: Unlike setting-autofailover.md, which gates nearly every advanced flag to Enterprise Edition, this page never once states whether auto-reprovisioning itself is Community or Enterprise only - a real silence given how heavily the sibling settings page uses that exact disclosure pattern. No default value is stated for --enabled or --max-nodes either.

cross_component_finding: A direct, textual copy-paste bug: the --enabled flag on THIS page (setting-autoreprovision) is described as 'Specifies whether or not auto-reprovisioning is enabled. Set this option to "1" to enable autofailover or "0" to disable autofailover.' - the flag help text names the wrong feature ('autofailover' instead of 'auto-reprovisioning'), almost certainly copy-pasted from setting-autofailover.md's --enable-auto-failover flag description ('Set this option to "1" to enable autofailover or "0" to disable autofailover.') without updating the feature name. This is direct, page-level evidence for this round's authorship-provenance hypothesis: a CLI-internal terminology drift caused by literal copy-paste across sibling subcommand pages, not merely boilerplate reuse of shared sections.
cross_product_finding: Not addressed on this page - no comparison to Capella, which manages ephemeral-bucket node-crash recovery internally with no customer-facing CLI equivalent to --max-nodes tuning.
